decisions.detail: 'Evaluate expressions that add, subtract, multiply or divide the trigonometric ratios of special angles, without using a calculator.' Only exercise evidence (19 items); the one rule failure of this chapter (rule 1).
decisions.basis: ORCHESTRATOR (AI) RULING, not a human stamp and not in the auto-pass rule set: section 5.6 never teaches combining the special-angle ratios in an expression. Its teaching text is a heading (EMA3S), one paragraph that introduces the special angles (b01716), the Pythagoras reminder (b01717), the two special triangles (b01718, b01719), the table of values for 30, 45 and 60 degrees (b01720) and the closing line 'These values are useful when we need to solve a problem involving trigonometric ratios without using a calculator' (b01721); there is no worked example in the section. That closing line is the only non-exercise text a finder cited for this skill, and the evidence check rightly refused it: it says why the values are useful, not how to evaluate a sum, difference, product or quotient of them. The method ('write each ratio using special angles, then simplify') appears only inside the worked answers of exercises Ex5-3:4-5 and Ex5-8:5-6, which are exercise evidence, not teaching evidence. The chapter summary (b01912) states only that the values can be found without a calculator. Rule 1 needs two different kinds and G1 can add no evidence, so the objective is dropped and each of its 19 exercise items is re-homed to lo:g10m5s6-1-1, the objective whose skill (the special-angle values in surd form, without a calculator) is the first step of every one of them. Ids: the dropped objective is the third of five, so the run's fourth and fifth objectives become lo:g10m5s6-1-3 and lo:g10m5s6-1-4.
